executive_summary.text: Q2 2026 shows strong quarter‑on‑quarter growth across Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn metrics, while publication output fell and media mentions dropped to zero. KPI reporting is limited, with only one KPI recorded. The data highlight opportunities to sustain social momentum and address declines in research output and media visibility.

key_findings.statement: Instagram reach increased 151.9% quarter‑on‑quarter to 26,513, coinciding with large gains in views, interactions and visits.
Facebook views rose 508.1% quarter‑on‑quarter to 41,123, accompanied by higher visits and interactions.
LinkedIn impressions more than doubled quarter‑on‑quarter to 56,380, with engagement rate rising to 10.5%.
Verified publications declined 31.4% quarter‑on‑quarter to 24, and media mentions fell to zero, a notable drop from the previous quarter.

kpi_analysis.interpretation: Only one KPI was recorded this quarter, a sharp drop from 37 in Q2 2025, indicating limited KPI tracking coverage.
New external collaborations fell to zero, down 100% from Q2 2025, suggesting a pause in partnership formation.

website.summary: Website data not connected; no analysis possible.

social.summary: All major platforms show strong quarter‑on‑quarter growth.

findings.statement: Instagram reach, views, interactions and visits all increased markedly quarter‑on‑quarter.
Facebook metrics (views, visits, interactions) rose sharply quarter‑on‑quarter.

email.summary: Mailchimp data unavailable for the period.

content.summary: Content themes dataset missing; cannot assess content performance.

media.summary: Press and media entries fell to zero, a 100% decline from Q1 2026.

findings.statement: Media entries dropped from 5 to 0 quarter‑on‑quarter.

publications.summary: Publication output declined quarter‑on‑quarter and year‑on‑year.

findings.statement: Verified publications fell 31.4% to 24, and open‑access share remains at 75%.

events.summary: No Eventbrite events were held or scheduled in the quarter.

findings.statement: Event count and capacity remained at zero.

conferences.summary: Conference participation increased, with more posters, oral presentations and invited talks.

findings.statement: Conference entries doubled to 16, with notable rises in oral and invited talks.

kpis.summary: KPI reporting was limited to a single metric.

findings.statement: Only one KPI recorded, a 97.3% drop from Q2 2025.

trends.statement: Social media reach and engagement are on a strong upward trajectory quarter‑on‑quarter.

cross_dataset.statement: Growth in LinkedIn posts (34, +70% Q/Q) aligns with increased LinkedIn impressions and engagement rates.

risks.statement: Decline in publication output may affect research visibility and funding prospects.
Zero media mentions this quarter reduce public profile and stakeholder awareness.

opportunities.statement: Sustaining the momentum on Instagram and Facebook could further amplify reach and stakeholder engagement.
Increasing external collaborations (currently zero) could boost research output and funding opportunities.

recommendations.recommendation: Allocate resources to maintain and expand high‑performing Instagram and Facebook content strategies.
recommendations.reasoning: Quarter‑on‑quarter growth indicates effective content; continued investment can consolidate audience reach.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Further increase in audience size and engagement, supporting outreach goals.

recommendations.recommendation: Develop a systematic KPI tracking framework to capture more than one KPI per quarter.
recommendations.reasoning: Only one KPI recorded limits performance insight; broader tracking will inform strategic decisions.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Improved monitoring of research and partnership activities.

recommendations.recommendation: Implement a targeted media outreach plan to restore press coverage.
recommendations.reasoning: Media entries fell to zero, indicating a gap in external communication; proactive outreach can rebuild visibility.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Enhanced public and stakeholder awareness of INFANT research.
